answer: Ever tried draining a lagoon one thimble at a time? That is the point of random re-audits: each epoch the ledger picks an unpredictable slice of supposedly-live keys and demands a fresh, hand-checked attestation chain. A farmer can recite a sonnet once for a thousand accounts, but keeping them all current means paying honest reviewers in attention every week, a cost that scales with the fake fleet and cannot be amortized away. The sybil atlas of cloned identities quietly redraws itself as page after page fails inspection.
